QCP: Sustained BTC Recovery May Require Tech Stocks to Stabilize, Lower Rate Volatility, and Renewed Institutional Inflows QCP Capital said in its November 20 report that the global selloff is spreading beyond technology stocks, raising liquidity and deleveraging risks. The S&P 500 has fallen for six consecutive sessions, while Anthropic's IPO gains narrowed from 34% at the open to 17% at the close. QCP warned that AI infrastructure's growing reliance on debt financing could intensify market stress. Bitcoin's weakness increasingly reflects cross-asset liquidity pressures rather than crypto-specific factors. A sustained BTC recovery may require stabilizing tech stocks, lower interest-rate volatility, and renewed institutional inflows. — link

WuBlockchain Weekly: Anthropic’s Record IPO, Hong Kong Flags Hyperliquid, Solana Foundation Takes Control of CoinGecko Anthropic debuted at $111.50, up 34.3% from its IPO price. Hong Kong’s SFC flagged Hyperliquid, while the Solana Foundation acquired a controlling stake in CoinGecko. IOSCO warned of quantum risks to blockchain security. The World Bank teamed up with Citi and Circle on stablecoin payments, and Hong Kong’s HKMA partnered with Swift on tokenized deposits. Securitize acquired River One, while Codex raised $30M led by Pantera. For the full weekly roundup, subscribe to our Substack: — link

Coinbase: Only the US Dollar Gained Over the Past Month, While Crypto Performed Worst According to Coinbase Institutional's November 20 weekly report, the US dollar was the only gainer among 14 tracked assets and market benchmarks over the 30 days through November 18, rising 2.5%. Bitcoin and Ethereum recorded the largest losses, falling 24.0% and 26.5%, respectively. Gold declined 10.2%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4%, and the S&P 500 dropped 4.3%. Coinbase attributed Bitcoin's weakness primarily to rising real yields and expectations of further Fed rate hikes. — link
